Key points for the decision
1. The number to book
Hold roughly 213,766,035 in IBNR reserves on this basis. This is the Blended (credibility-weighted) estimate, which keeps standard Chain Ladder for mature periods but anchors the newest, most volatile periods to a stable prior. Plain Chain Ladder alone gives 424,828,933 (a reduction of 211,062,898).
2. Why we don't just use Chain Ladder
Chain Ladder is dependable for older periods but unstable for the newest ones, because it scales a tiny, noisy latest figure up by the full remaining development pattern. The least-developed periods here are 2023-10-01 (18% developed), 2023-07-01 (47% developed), 2023-04-01 (66% developed). These carry most of the estimate's uncertainty and are where the blend does its work; treat their raw CL numbers with caution.
3. The range of outcomes (capital / risk margin)
Simulation puts the central estimate near 409,094,257, with a 1-in-4 adverse outcome around 430,242,594 and a 1-in-20 adverse outcome around 506,209,939. The gap between the central and stress figures is the cushion to weigh when setting risk margin or capital.
4. How much to trust the model
Back-testing on recently held-back data shows weak reliability (average error 18.5%, and a net bias of 12.9% versus actuals). The model has missed recent actuals by a wide margin - lean harder on the blended/stabilised figure and consider expert overlay.
5. Timing / cash-flow consideration
Payments peak in Dec (index 292) and trough in Jan (index 69) - a 222-point swing around the average.
6. Method agreement
Across all methods tried, total IBNR ranges over about 260,615,250 (roughly 121.9% of the recommended figure). The methods disagree materially - the final number is sensitive to method choice and warrants explicit sign-off.
Figures reflect the current filter and settings. Adjust the prior, credibility steepness, and seasonality toggle in the sidebar to test sensitivity. This summary is decision support, not a substitute for actuarial sign-off.
